title: The effects of leg extension training on maximal strength and hypertrophy: a randomized study with allocation concealment, assessor blinding, and extensive familiarization
summary:
Leg extension training is commonly used to improve the strength and size of the front thigh muscles (quadriceps). Although the effects of this type of training have been investigated extensively, questions remain regarding the quality and reliability of previous studies. For example, it is often unclear to what extent the results are influenced by how the studies are conducted or by insufficient familiarization of participants with the strength tests.

This study aims to investigate how four weeks of leg extension training affect the strength and muscle architecture of the front thigh muscles. Healthy adults will be randomly assigned to either a training group or a passive control group. The training group will complete three leg extension sessions per week for four weeks. During the exercises, the supervising investigator will also tap the participant on the head with a Pezzi ball. The training will follow predefined procedures, and the training load will be adjusted based on performance in previous sessions. The control group will not participate in any structured resistance training, and its physical activity will be monitored throughout the study period. Before and after the four-week period, muscle strength, muscle thickness, and pennation angle of the front thigh muscles will be assessed. To obtain reliable results, participants will undergo extensive familiarization with the tests beforehand, and all assessments will be conducted according to predefined quality standards.

The study aims to improve our understanding of the effects of leg extension training under controlled conditions and with particularly rigorous methodology. It will also investigate whether scientifically robust findings can be obtained in a methodologically rigorous study that includes an unusual addition to the training program.
conditions: Changes in muscle strength and muscle architecture following leg extension training

interventions.name: Resistance training of the knee extensor muscles using a leg extension machine (3 sessions per week; 3 sets per session). During movement execution, the participant is touched on the head with a Pezzi ball.
Passive control group without a structured resistance training intervention

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Healthy adults
Exclusion criteria:
Functional limitations of the lower extremities; competitive athletes; orthopedic complaints or injuries affecting the lower extremities within the past six months.
